text:
maria_sales: Hey team — FinServe sent over a security questionnaire and a POC ask. Key points: they require BYO-HSM/CMK, EU+US key residency, automated rotation with 30-day rotation window (they may shorten), audit log retention 7 years, and an SLA of 99.95% with 15 min RTO for key recovery. They also want an estimate for cost uplift for Dedicated + HSM throughput ~2k req/s. POC target: 4 weeks. Can eng/sec/finance weigh in?

ben_soleng: Thanks Maria. Quick clarifying q's: which KMS vendors are they planning to bring (AWS CloudHSM, Azure HSM, Google Cloud HSM)? And is key material going to live in their tenant? We support two modes: 1) kms-integration where we call their KMS for envelope encryption, 2) TLS-wrapped HSMs via our connector.

rahul_cust: They prefer AWS CloudHSM for primary and want a failover to an EU HSM cluster (either AWS or Azure). Keys must never be exported in plaintext.

sarah_sec: We can support CMKs backed by customer HSMs. Details: we perform envelope encryption — Redwood holds only wrapped DEKs, not plaintext CMKs. Supported features: HSM-backed CMKs (AWS CloudHSM), key-wrapping via RSA-OAEP or AES-KW, rotation hooks (webhook or scheduler), JWK export for audit, and signed attestations. We do not retain key material.

alex_finance: For pricing ballpark (subject to SOW): Dedicated base + BYO-HSM add-on. Rough numbers: Base Dedicated commit $12,000/mo, BYO-HSM integration + premium for HSM routing and key attestation $4,500/mo, HSM throughput surcharge (2k req/s) + burst reserve ~$3,000/mo, optional emergency key escrow service (manual, > SLA) $2,000/mo. One-time POC integration engineering fee estimates: $25k–$40k depending on network complexity. Will confirm after eng triage.

jordan_eng: POC workstream I suggest: 
1) Week 0: Kickoff, NDA review, contact ops, and network prescreen.
2) Week 1: Connectivity & handshake — exchange certs, open firewall rules, test mutual TLS to their KMS endpoints.
3) Week 2: Integrate key wrapping calls and run functional tests (rotate keys via our rotation API).
4) Week 3: Load tests (synthetic traffic to validate 2k req/s; KV cache/latency impacts).
5) Week 4: Failover and RTO drills, runbook handoff, logs & attestation delivery.

I can drop a sample config we use for BYO-KMS connector: 
```json
{
  "kms_provider": "aws-cloudhsm",
  "endpoint": "https://kms-connector.customer.example:8443",
  "auth": { "type": "mTLS", "cert": "---BEGIN CERT---" },
  "wrap_algo": "RSA-OAEP",
  "key_id": "alias/redwood-prod-cmk"
}
```

maria_sales: Perfect. Sarah — quick Q on rotation automation: customer wants 30-day rotation and immediate revocation path. Can we support scheduled rotations + immediate revoke with < 15 min propagation?

sarah_sec: Yes — scheduled rotations are supported. Propagation to caches: we push invalidation events to all serving nodes; typical propagation is < 2 minutes for control plane invalidation, but KV caches might still serve prefetched prefixes until TTL expiry. For strict immediate revocation you can: 1) reduce cache TTLs for sensitive routes during the POC; 2) use forced key revocation which invalidates prefix/KV caches and triggers a cold-call to KMS. Forced revocation end-to-end measured ~8–12s in our lab, but depends on active batching windows. Note: forced revocation increases latency temporarily.

rahul_cust: Good to hear. They also asked about audit log retention and format — JSON logs with signed attestations?

sarah_sec: We emit audit logs via your S3/GCS bucket or push to your SIEM (syslog/stackdriver). Logs include key_id, operation, caller_identity, request_id, and HSM attestation blob (base64). We can sign attestations with our platform key and include HSM-supplied attestation when available. Retention configurable; 7 years is fine via object lifecycle policy on your storage.

alex_finance: For the POC quote I recommend we propose a 3-month trial commit at 50% of the monthly Dedicated base to cover infra + support, plus the one-time integration fees. That gets them to an expedited SLA and priority on on-call.

ben_soleng: Blockers to call out for the customer: 1) Network — customer must open egress to our connector endpoints and allow inbound mTLS from our connector if they host the HSM gateway on-prem. 2) HSM throughput — we need to align on expected operations (encrypt vs decrypt ratios, key lifecycle ops). 3) Legal — escrow exception if they want us to hold backup keys. 4) Timezone ops window for ceremony — they require key ceremony during EU business hours.

maria_sales: Rahul — can you confirm whether the CloudHSM cluster will be provisioned by their infra team or if they want Redwood to spin up connectors in their VPC? Also confirm legal on escrow.

rahul_cust: They will provision CloudHSM clusters in their accounts and can provide a peered VPC. Legal will review escrow and likely prefer customer-only escrow unless required for DR. We should assume no escrow for now.

jordan_eng: Action items: 
- jordan_eng: create POC runbook + checklist (by EOD Fri).
- ben_soleng: write integration playbook and sample config for their infra (by Mon).
- alex_finance: draft POC commercial (3-month trial numbers + one-time fees) and share with maria (tomorrow).
- sarah_sec: prepare security addendum language for BYO-HSM and audit log schema (48h).
- rahul_cust: confirm CloudHSM provisioning details and whether they can open a peered VPC (by Mon).

ops_bot: @channel POC created: ticket#POC-4822 — onboarding checklist assigned to jordan_eng, ben_soleng. See https://redwood.internal/pocs/POC-4822

maria_sales: Thanks all. If no blockers we’ll propose kickoff next Tues. :thumbsup:
